answer: A memory-hard challenge protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to hold large pseudorandom tables in high-speed RAM. Verifiers emit an interrogation pulse, requiring rapid memory proofs within latency bounds locked to quartz clocks. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of scarce physical RAM per identity, unable to hide virtual clones behind an onyx veil of shared servers. However, this bandwidth barrier disadvantages legitimate lightweight agents on constrained devices.
